Hi Olivia — great speaking with you and the Medinova team earlier. Summary and next steps below (TL;DR up front).

TL;DR:
- Redwood can sign a BAA. I attached our most recent BAA template (redwood_baa_template_v2.pdf) and asked Legal to prioritize Medinova-specific edits.
- PHI-eligible hosting modes: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC or on-prem) are supported for PHI. Our hosted multi-tenant API is NOT approved for PHI without a dedicated deployment and contractual controls.
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope for production inference (report available under NDA). We usually provide an encrypted download link via our security portal; Marcus below will share the link and next steps for the RFI.
- KMS/HSM: We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and offer optional HSM for Private deployments.

Action items / timeline:
1) Marcus will upload SOC 2 artifacts and a short runbook for Dedicated/Private setups to the shared link by EOD 6/5.
2) Priya will send our BAA template and confirm any clauses commonly redlined by healthcare customers (we can highlight them). Expect the BAA template now (attached) and a suggested change-log by 6/6.
3) Medinova completes the vendor RFI and returns it — that will accelerate procurement and security sign-off.

Notes / details:
- Eligible deployment modes for PHI: 
  * Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation, network controls, and optional private peering. Suitable for most PHI use cases if the contract includes BAA and required security controls.
  * Private (VPC or on-prem): Full isolation; preferred when customers require data to stay in a customer-managed network or in a specific region/country. Support for air-gapped on-prem packages is available for regulated scenarios.
  * Hosted API (multi-tenant): Not approved for PHI by default. We can discuss an enterprise-hosted carve-out but that generally looks like Dedicated or Private under the hood.

- Data residency: For Dedicated and Private we can provision capacity in specific cloud regions. For EU residency we recommend Private VPC with region pinning; for multi-region workflows we provide routing policies but data movement for PHI must be scoped contractually.

- SOC 2 evidence & RFI: we share an encrypted SOC 2 bundle under NDA. Marcus will provide the download link and a brief checklist mapping the RFI questions to our controls.

If helpful, we can schedule a 20-min security sync tomorrow (6/6) to walk your RFI with Marcus and Priya. 

Thanks —

Hi Olivia / Tessa — attaching the SOC 2 download and a brief mapping doc (I uploaded both to our secure artifact portal). Link: https://secure.redwood.ai/artifacts/download/SOC2-Med-5932 (access requires the NDA token; I sent that to Olivia via the portal).

Quick notes on questions we see frequently on RFI items: 
- Encryption in transit & at rest: yes. TLS 1.2+ for transit; AES-256 for data at rest. For Dedicated and Private we can enable customer-managed keys.
- Logging / auditability: all inference requests include request/response metadata in audit logs, with token-level cost breakdowns accessible via the Console. For PHI we recommend enabling extended retention and forwarding logs to a customer-managed SIEM.
- Data minimization / retention: Default retention window for inference artifacts is 30 days; we can configure shorter retention or disable persistent logs for Private deployments per contract.
- Background processing: Redwood does not use customer content for model training. That is disallowed in the BAA and standard Data Processing terms.

Attached: medinova_vendor_rfi.xlsx (with cell-level comments completed inline) and a short mapping file (RFI->control references). I left a few questions for Medinova security to confirm (highlighted in yellow).

Planned timeline if Medinova returns the RFI this week: SOC 2 artifacts shared (done), BAA review cycle start (Priya to send draft 6/6), legal & procurement kickoff (target week of 6/14).

—Marcus
